text:
maria: Quick follow-up on the RBAC precompute RFC — I want to put a concrete decomposition and cutover plan on the table for feedback.

alex: +1. main risk i see is cold-start latency for tenants that aren't in the precompute set.

maria: Right. My sketch: split authz into two paths — an "edge precompute" fast-path that answers collection/route-level allow lists, and an "inline authoritative" path for anything that needs row-level checks or on-miss resolution. Misses fall back synchronously. Target miss-rate <2%.

sam: Do we have data on current hot tenants / miss distribution? that will shape sizing for the edge cache.

maria: I sampled last night. summary: top 20% tenants account for ~85% requests. authz median ~12ms, p95 ~45ms. I ran a simple aggregation: ```sql
SELECT tenant_id, count(*) as cnt FROM request_logs WHERE ts > now() - interval '7 days' GROUP BY tenant_id ORDER BY cnt DESC LIMIT 100;```

taylor: Sounds promising. Important caveat: precompute can only handle ACLs that are independent of the query content. row-level predicates still need inline checks. we must be explicit about scope.

alex: Invalidation is the other big one. role/permission churn must propagate quickly. suggest changefeed -> pubsub -> edge invalidation with a version token. if version mismatch, edge forces synchronous re-eval.

maria: Agreed. Proposed phases: 1) build precompute batch job + changefeed hook for immediate invalidation; 2) add LRU edge cache with small TTL (5m) + version tokens; 3) cut over per-region using canary (10% -> 50% -> 100%).

sam: Rollout plan: start with a low-risk dashboard (analytics-team read-only) at 1% traffic for 48h, compare latency, error rates, and authz miss traces. metric guardrails: authz-error-rate <0.01%, p95 latency not increased.

devops-bot: deployment note: new precompute service branch (feature/rbac-edge) must pass staging perf tests before scheduling prod deploy.

taylor: From perf sims, prefilter reduces query fanout ~30% for common dashboards but increases small authz RPCs. we'll need token-level cost breakdowns in console telemetry to detect regressions.

maria: I'll own the RFC follow-up doc and checklist. owners: maria (design + rollout), alex (invalidation + infra), sam (metrics + canary), taylor (QA + security review).

alex: can we add an automated eval that compares a sample of query outputs between precompute-path and authoritative-path to catch any correctness gaps?

maria: Yes — will add a nightly regression job that replays 1M recent queries through both paths and diffs permits + responses. will also include a short prompt set for manual audit.

sam: SGTM. once we have perf numbers from staging i'll open the canary PR.

maria: cool. i'll post the follow-up doc link here once written and tag owners. thanks folks :thumbsup:
